correctness.rationale: For each nonzero c with -c nonsquare, degree two Capelli/tower reduction gives A(T)^2+c irreducible iff discriminant x+4alpha is a nonsquare in F_{q^2}. The norm gives x^2+16c, never zero. Summing (1-chi(x^2+16c))/2 across all a,b gives q(q+1)/2. Two distinct eligible constants yield q/4 [q+2+sum_x chi((x^2+16c)(x^2+16d))]. Replace x^2=t with multiplicity 1+chi(t): the pure quadratic sum equals -1, and the cubic sum is the trace sum for Y^2=X(X+c)(X+d). Distinct roots establish ellipticity; rational 2-torsion gives integral q#E/4; Hasse gives strict positivity. The independent exact polynomial-gcd checker passed 74 cases across 10 fields, but does not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: A natural two-shift irreducibility question for degree-four compositional families is completely classified for all odd finite fields, not just tested small cases. The nontrivial exact count equals one fourth q times a genus-one rational-point count, so its variation is governed by Frobenius; rational 2-torsion and Hasse show simultaneous irreducibles exist for every locally admissible pair, even small fields. The explicit singular/diagonal cases complete the classification. This is more than a routine polynomial reparameterization of the large-field twin-irreducibility asymptotic.
